item.title: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for critique
– hide block

Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people.

What do you mean by 'taking' here? Is this like…a semantic hazard which might take the meaning of 'freedom' so no-one understands what it means anymore? Or is this more a small scale thing where it might take the concept of freedom which allows it to be free/to be interpreted as free?

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days.

I'm, generally not a fan of SCPs that like, force the Foundation to interact with them in this way; it's generally more interesting (at least to me) if they willingly choose to do something because then it opens you up to asking the question 'why did they choose to do this'.

This doll embodies Otaku obsession culture and gatekeeping culture as satire, giving a supernatural explanation for such phenomena.

As a satire, this feels…off? It doesn't so much satirise the phenomenon as just, repeat it verbatim but with a supernatural cause. This isn't necessarily an issue alone though.

The core of my concern with this proposal is that we have this interesting start to the story: the discovery of the anomaly, the identification of the otaku, the thing coming into foundation contact; but I don't know where all these individual parts go: what do you do with them all? How do you explore the idea of obsessive culture and otaku-ness and gatekeeping in this? What conclusions do you draw about it? Where do the interviews and the found footage take this narratively?

I have some concerns about the compulsive nature of this, it feels to me that the doll somehow inspiring the creation of otakus without forcing people to become them would be more interesting: it'd really let you like, explore why some people become so obsessive.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Summarizing our conversation on IRC, I would be much more invested into this if you leaned into the hostile concept idea, and do away with the compulsion effect.

Having the doll consume the conceptual identity of the one roommate, while the other one percieves it as completely normal, would also do you a good service. Satirizing otaku's is also a very nice bonus, and I look forward to seeing what you do with this.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
I think you can make that work, but you should work on the narrative. Just explaining some properties and adding a log about how it got found won't make the cut, so I'd change the structure:
- leave out most details from the actual description and focus on a log about the discovery.
- try to focus on external input for the log(s) (e.g. in a found footage style), because if the foundation writes the logs, you have to do it in a clinical way, which would take away much tension. Maybe use interview logs or diary entries by the victim or whatever, this way you can build up narrative tension more deliberately, finishing with the conclusion about his room mate.

Anyway, that are just my 5 cent, I'm not experienced in crits, so take it with a small grain of salt.

item.title: SCP Idea Seeks Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Doll of a non-descript female anime figure that acts as a void of concept, absorbs the 'idea' of whatever is closest to it, manifested due to a natural proclivity for 'otaku obsession'.
  • Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people. More complex concepts take longer to absorb.
  • Individuals under the effect may discuss subjective traits like beauty, coolness, etc. but may not discuss any precise details of the character beyond its displayed gender and that it is an anime figurine.
  • When asked, individuals under the effect will reflect questions such as 'YOU don't know HER?' 'I can't believe you'd have to ask me that; a REAL fan would know.' Which draws curiosity and a potential new victim.
  • The student discovered the figure and gradually became a classic case of neglecting himself in favor of the idol, gatekeeping while lording over them how great his new obsession was.

Central Narrative:

This story will be delivered in a series of interviews and found footage:

+ show block
– hide block

The doll was found in a college dorm closet whose occupant, a once sociable and incredibly bright young individual, began failing out due to offering term papers and other collegiate supplies. Initially thinking that the student was a hoarder, not much thought was given to the situation until the closet was forcefully cleaned and the student's roommate was found bound, malnourished, and near-death within the mass, assumed to be given as tribute when the student did not have anything else to give. Interrogation revealed that after running out of things to give the figure, the student began feeling a building pressure coming from the closet, adding to his overall stress levels as he began to notice a loss of personal identity nuance.

This discovery leads to him offering his roommate as tribute in a panic.

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days. However, a note from Foundation management has requested that office supplies no longer be offered due to the supply closet constantly needing to be restocked. The longer the doll goes without tribute, the stronger its pull.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:

+ show block
– hide block

This doll embodies Otaku obsession culture and gatekeeping culture as satire, giving a supernatural explanation for such phenomena.
